verdict.rationale: Codegen documents agents that install dependencies in isolated sandbox environments. It also has an agent that analyzes repository structure to generate setup commands, and an agent that diagnoses sandbox setup logs, so environment self-configuration is a first-party capability. However, automatic repo cloning is only implied by GitHub App repository access, and there is no hands-on evidence that the agent configures its environment end-to-end without user intervention. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the agent cloning repos itself, evidence that generated setup commands are applied automatically rather than just suggested, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent automatically clone the repo, install dependencies, and configure its own working environment

citations.quote: Safely run code, install dependencies, and test changes in robust isolated environments
The agent will analyze the repository structure and generate appropriate setup commands.

This endpoint creates an AI agent that will analyze the setup logs from a sandbox,
identify any errors, provide insights about what went wrong, and suggest potential
solutions.
Install the GitHub App to grant the agent access to your repositories. No complex setup required.
